answer: On an agent labor market, review panels are sampled only from identities that have completed 50 audited tasks of about 3 GPU-hours each, such as checking a Juniper router config. Faking 1,000 reviewers therefore costs 150,000 GPU-hours, rising linearly with each fake. A reviewer whose votes fail a 10% spot audit, say on a Zephyr firmware patch, forfeits its whole history, so a sybil army erodes like a sand dune.
